metadata.analysisPurpose: Extract and specify patterns for automated verification and testing

error_handling.description: Pattern for synchronous error handling with explicit error types

examples.code: if (b === 0) { throw new Error('Division by zero'); }

if (n < 0) { throw new Error('Factorial of negative number'); }
if (!Number.isInteger(n)) { throw new Error('Factorial requires integer input'); }
if (n < 0) { throw new Error('Cannot calculate square root of negative number'); }

rule_1.name: All division operations check for zero divisor
rule_1.assertion: Find all functions accepting division/modulo operations. Verify they contain guard clause: if (divisor === 0) { throw ... }
checkableConditions: Function contains guard clause before division/modulo
Guard clause uses === operator (not just truthiness)
Error message is descriptive

rule_2.name: All mathematical constraints are validated
rule_2.assertion: Functions like factorial, sqrt should validate domain constraints (negative numbers, non-integers)
checkableConditions: Preconditions checked before computation
Errors thrown with specific error messages
Error messages explain the constraint violated

rule_3.name: Error messages are user-friendly
rule_3.assertion: All thrown errors contain meaningful context
checkableConditions: Error message explains what went wrong
Error message suggests why it happened
No generic 'Error: Error' messages

programmaticChecks.name: Check for unguarded division
programmaticChecks.description: Find division/modulo operations without preceding zero-check

programmaticChecks.name: Verify error constructors
programmaticChecks.description: Verify all thrown errors are constructed properly

programmaticChecks.name: Check error message specificity
programmaticChecks.description: Extract and validate error messages contain specific context

automationFeasibility.reason: Error-handling patterns are deterministic and syntactically verifiable
automationFeasibility.implementation: Create linting rules in ESLint that verify guard clauses precede operations

async_patterns.description: Pattern for asynchronous operations and promises

rule_1.name: All async functions have proper error handling
rule_1.assertion: Every async function either has try-catch or returns Promise that is awaited with catch
checkableConditions: Function marked as async
Contains try-catch block OR calling function has .catch()
Error handler provides meaningful logging
Error doesn't silently fail

rule_2.name: Await is used on all promises
rule_2.assertion: No promises are created without await unless explicitly handled
checkableConditions: All new Promise() or async calls have await
No orphaned promises without .catch() handling
Promise.all/race are awaited

rule_3.name: Fallback/caching patterns for network operations
rule_3.assertion: Network operations have offline fallback strategies
checkableConditions: Catch block implements fallback (cache, default data, retry)
Cache strategy is documented
Graceful degradation is evident

programmaticChecks.name: Find async functions without try-catch
programmaticChecks.description: Async functions should contain try-catch or ensure error handling

programmaticChecks.name: Verify await on promise-returning calls
programmaticChecks.pattern: AST: FunctionCall where returns Promise but not awaited
programmaticChecks.description: Promises should be awaited unless explicitly handled

programmaticChecks.name: Check for catch handlers at module level
programmaticChecks.description: Top-level async functions should have catch handlers

automationFeasibility.reason: Async patterns are mostly syntactic but require control flow analysis for completeness
automationFeasibility.implementation: Create ESLint rules for async best practices; use TypeScript's Promise type checking

test_structure.description: Pattern for test organization and assertion patterns

features: Regression tests with explicit non-matching assertion
Function wrapped in arrow function for expect
Error case in same describe block

rule_1.name: All functions have corresponding tests
rule_1.assertion: Every exported function in src/ has at least 2-3 test cases
checkableConditions: Function is exported from src file
Tests exist in tests/ directory
Test name matches function name
Multiple test cases cover different scenarios

rule_2.name: Error cases are explicitly tested
rule_2.assertion: Functions that throw errors have test cases for those errors
checkableConditions: For each throw statement, there's a test with expect().toThrow()
Error message is verified
Both error condition and normal path tested

rule_3.name: Test structure follows describe/test hierarchy
rule_3.assertion: Tests are organized with nested describe blocks for grouping
checkableConditions: Top-level describe for module/class
Nested describe for function grouping
Descriptive test names explaining what is tested
Consistent indentation and structure

rule_4.name: Regression tests explicitly prevent known bugs
rule_4.assertion: When bugs are discovered, regression tests are added
checkableConditions: Test name contains 'regression' or indicates a specific bug
Test includes both positive and negative assertions
Comment explains the bug being prevented

programmaticChecks.name: Check describe/test structure
programmaticChecks.pattern: AST: Verify structure matches describe->test hierarchy
programmaticChecks.description: Tests should use describe blocks for organization

programmaticChecks.name: Verify error testing pattern
programmaticChecks.description: Count error test cases vs error-throwing functions

programmaticChecks.name: Check for regression test markers
programmaticChecks.description: Identify regression tests and defensive assertions

automationFeasibility.reason: Test structure is highly standardized and syntactically checkable
automationFeasibility.implementation: Create tools to verify test coverage, test naming conventions, and error case coverage

activity_composition.description: Pattern for composing complex activities from tasks and dependencies

features: Linear dependency chain (verify -> read -> generate -> test -> commit -> deploy)
Diamond dependency pattern (two parents generating different outputs before merge)
Multiple impulse types (memo, execution traces, metrics, patterns)

rule_1.name: All task dependencies are resolvable
rule_1.assertion: Every dependency references a task that exists and comes before it
checkableConditions: Task ID matches a defined task
Dependency task appears earlier in tasks array
No circular dependencies
No forward references

rule_2.name: Impulses are properly configured with budget
rule_2.assertion: Every impulse has budget and priority defined
checkableConditions: Budget is positive integer
Priority is one of: critical, high, medium, low
Type is valid (memo, file, activityOutput, etc.)
Optional impulses are marked as optional: true

rule_3.name: Tasks have proper validation and error handling
rule_3.assertion: Each task defines validation rules or error handling
checkableConditions: Command tasks have exitCode validation
Prompt tasks have requiredOutputs
Retry strategy defined for risky operations
Timeout values are reasonable

rule_4.name: Output schema matches activity produces
rule_4.assertion: Activity outputSchema.produces matches the shapes produced by tasks
checkableConditions: Output shape is defined in outputSchema
All produces are realistic given task outputs
Conditions for each produce are clear
Structure matches expected data format

rule_5.name: Learning configuration is present
rule_5.assertion: Activities define how they contribute to learning system
checkableConditions: tracing.recordTrace is configured
tracing.contributeToLearning is set
learning.onSuccess or onFailure handlers exist
Autonomy section present for self-directed activities

programmaticChecks.name: Verify task dependency DAG
programmaticChecks.description: Ensure no circular dependencies and all refs valid

programmaticChecks.name: Check impulse budget allocation
programmaticChecks.description: Verify impulses don't exceed context budget

programmaticChecks.name: Verify task validation rules
programmaticChecks.pattern: Schema validation: each task.validation matches task.type
programmaticChecks.description: Command tasks need exitCode, Prompt tasks need output validation

programmaticChecks.name: Check variable interpolation
programmaticChecks.description: Find all template variables and verify they're provided

automationFeasibility.reason: Activity structure is JSON-based and schema-validatable; dependencies are graph-checkable
automationFeasibility.implementation: Create activity validator that checks schema, dependency graph, impulse budgets, and variable interpolation

automationFeasibility.reasoning: All four patterns are highly automatable due to their structured nature

Build test coverage verification and naming convention tools

Implement ESLint rules plus TypeScript type checking

key_findings.async_patterns_quality: Proper try-catch usage with fallback strategies (caching), good error propagation
key_findings.test_coverage_quality: Comprehensive test structure with nested describes, regression tests, error case coverage
key_findings.activity_composition_maturity: Well-structured task dependencies, proper impulse budgeting, learning system integration
